newsitem.title: UK: John Laing rises after upbeat statement.
newsitem.headline: John Laing rises after upbeat statement.

text.p: Shares in construction group John Laing Plc rose on Thursday after the company posted a drop in first-half profits but said there were signs of recovery ahead.

The stock was up 13-1/2p at 258 by 1439 GMT in thin trading of just 10,000 shares. Other construction stocks also rose, with Alfred McAlpine up 5p at 157-1/2 and Morrison Construction up 6p at 172-1/2.
"There is clear evidence that, in recent months, the South East homes market has begun to improve," said chairman Martin Laing, "and we are now seeing price rises in many of our developments."
Laing said pre-tax profit dropped to 8.8 million stg in the six months to June 30 from 9.7 million a year before.

"The elusive feel good factor seems to be returning," Laing said. "The construction market is, in profit terms, showing some very early indications of recovery but margins can often lag behind contract awards."
"I believe that the prospects for our business are more promising than they have been for some years."
Laing said it is in talks for the M40 road contract and a hospital in Norwich funded under the UK government's Private Finance Initiative.
